- Tiered discount schedule (commitment thresholds and corresponding discounts)
- Small scope edit to the SOW calendar (move kickoff window from Q3 to mid-July)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that's faster.

1) Discount breakpoints: is procurement asking for increasing % discount on committed spend (e.g., 10% at $X, 15% at $Y) or flat unit price tiers? If you can share the target numbers we will mirror them in the Order Form and show the modeled effective rates.

2) SOW timing: you mentioned shifting kickoff to mid-July — is the preference a hard date or a flexible window (2–4 weeks)? That affects our resource allocation.

We'll produce a marked-up Order Form and a short summary of material MSA conflicts to speed procurement/legal review. Expect our first pass by Monday EOD PT.

If helpful, Karthik and I can do a 20-min sync Monday morning to walk procurement through the breaks.

Nora — quick note from sales: procurement typically prefers milestone-style tiers tied to committed spend rather than perpetual per-unit pricing. To make the economics transparent for your CFO we propose the following illustrative table (we'll put exact numbers in the Order Form once you confirm targets):

- Tier A: 0–$250K/year — base list pricing
- Tier B: $250K–$750K/year — 12% off list
- Tier C: $750K+ / year — 18% off list

If procurement needs 12/24/36 month commitment versions, we can show a blended effective rate for each term. Also: we can offer a 60-day price-protection clause for any scale-driven changes during the first contract year.

Would procurement be comfortable with those discount levels as a starting point? If yes, I'll ask finance to include an internal margin check and we'll mark it in the Order Form.

Irene — looping Rishi since this touches quota recognition and any deal-specific concessions.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Order form — tiered discounts & SOW edits

Hi all — I reviewed the Vitalsense Order Form and attached a redline (redlines_neha_v1.docx). Highlights / open items:

- Discount mechanics: acceptable to model tiered % off list. We'll need a clear definition of "committed spend" (prepaid vs. invoiced) and an annual true-up clause.
- MSA conflicts: Section 5.2 of the Order Form attempts to override MSA data-retention terms — we should keep the MSA as the priority and reflect the 12-month retention as an Order Form operational requirement, not a contractual divergence.
- Price protection: I can accept a 60-day price-protection window, but we should limit retroactive credits to True-ups only (no retroactive additional discounts beyond agreed tiers).
- PO requirement: If Vitalsense requires a PO with specific payment terms, include a PO reference field in the Order Form and indicate that invoicing will reference that PO number.

Next steps: I've tracked the redlines and added comments where I need procurement confirmation (committed spend definition and PO timing). Please review the doc and let me know if procurement can commit to the spend definition by COB Tue (May 5).

Neha Kapoor
Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
